summary: Ingress fan-in causing runtime watchdog resets and elevated 5xx across tenant during burst
description:
Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-13 02:12 UTC NimbleDocs reported a sudden spike in 5xx responses for their tenant during an ingestion burst. Impact: ~35% of requests returned 5xx over a 20 minute window; streaming sessions dropped with 'upstream reset' errors. Environment: prod (us-east-1), customer on Dedicated capacity pool D-42. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send high-rate concurrent short requests (1-3 request/sec per connection) with many small sequences (<=64 tokens) during a tenant ramp. 2) Observe rapid connection fan-in at ingress. 3) Watch for runtime timeouts and 5xx responses. Observed logs:
- api-gateway: "proxy: upstream reset by peer" spikes correlated with accept queue depth > 1200
- runtime: watchdog: "worker exceeded max_idle_time, resetting" and "kvcache eviction thrash"
- autoscaler: multiple rapid scale events then a stall
Frequency: Intermittent, reproducible during simulated tenant bursts
Impacted customer flows: inference API, short streaming sessions
Additional context: Customer was performing a controlled traffic ramp tied to a nightly batch ingestion. They reported the issue had started after a small config change on their side to increase concurrency per client.
comments: 2026-03-13 02:28 - Support (Olivia): Received customer report, validated spike in 5xx on tenant D-42. Asked for request IDs and their ramp script. Escalated to SRE and runtime-oncall.

2026-03-13 03:05 - SRE (Ethan): Observed correlated accept_queue and keepalive spikes on the API gateway. Multiple downstream runtimes reported watchdog resets. Captured runtime logs and traced a sequence where rapid new connections triggered prefetch queue contention.

2026-03-13 03:27 - Runtime Eng (Maya): Heap and GPU memory stable; runtime threads show repeated soft watchdog restarts with backtrace pointing to internal timer reset path when per-connection throughput is high. Noted kvcache eviction events immediate prior to reset.

2026-03-13 04:10 - Support (Olivia): Sent customer temporary mitigation: throttle client concurrency to 50% and enable connection pooling. Customer confirmed partial relief but still seeing elevated error floor at peak.

2026-03-13 11:42 - Customer (NimbleDocs - Rahul): Provided ramp script and sample request IDs. Confirmed they reverted their concurrency change and observed reduced 5xx but want a long-term fix so scheduled production runs not blocked.

2026-03-14 09:15 - SRE (Ethan): Applied temporary ingress rate-smoothing at edge (10s token bucket) for D-42 to damp fan-in. Error rate dropped to baseline. Planning deeper root cause analysis and durable fixes.
2026-03-14 12:30 - Runtime Eng (Maya): Experimenting with backoff in prefetch queue handling and extending watchdog window as a Canary on a small subset of nodes.
investigation_notes: Metrics observed: 5xx rate peaked at 37% for tenant D-42 between 02:12-02:32 UTC; api-gateway accept_queue length >1200; runtime prefetch queue depth spiked to >2000 on several hosts.
Runtime logs: repeated 'watchdog: worker exceeded max_idle_time, resetting' messages correlated with prefetch queue GC and kvcache eviction bursts.
Hypothesis 1: Connection fan-in causes rapid scheduling pressure on runtime thread pool; prefetch/kvcache eviction amplifies latency, watchdog fires and restarts worker leading to 5xx.
Hypothesis 2: Autoscaler oscillation during burst creates node churn; new nodes not fully warmed for KV cache causing eviction storms and transient runtime failures.
Evidence: Warmup metrics show high model cold starts on nodes added during the window; kv cache hit rate fell from 94% to 62% during spike.

Reproduction steps used by SRE: synthetic burst script (provided by customer) + added guardrails on staging cluster; reproduced error floor and watchdog resets consistently when concurrency per client > 300 and accept_queue sustained.
Potential risk: If left unmitigated, other tenants performing similar ramps could trigger cascading errors due to shared gateway accept queues and autoscaler behavior.
resolution: Temporary mitigation applied: ingress rate-smoothing token bucket (10s window) enabled for tenant D-42 which reduced immediate 5xx to baseline.
Workaround documented for customer: enable client-side connection pooling, cap concurrent connections per instance and stagger ramp-ups; recommended configuration attached.

Planned next steps: 1) runtime team to implement soft backpressure in prefetch path to avoid eviction storms, 2) autoscaler tuning to increase warmup buffer and reduce rapid node churn, 3) improve gateway accept_queue telemetry and per-tenant dampening logic.

Owner assignments: runtime backpressure fix (Maya), autoscaler warmup tuning (Liam), gateway dampening feature (Ethan). Target: rollout canary changes by 2026-03-20 and monitor error floor for two full weekday production peaks.
Follow-up: Postmortem to be created if a repeat incident occurs; add test case to chaos harness to simulate high fan-in ramps.
